title: What is known about 1RB---_1LC0LC_1RD1LB_1LE1RD_0LA1LF_1LD0RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_1LC0LC_1RD1LB_1LE1RD_0LA1LF_1LD0RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, with strong evidence that it never halts. The tape is a list of blocks of 1s; the head alternates between a pass to the right that erases every other block and a sweep to the left that rebuilds them. Lean proves these block rules for all block lengths, and that the sweep meeting a gap of exactly four 0s halts; reading the table backwards, that is the only way to the halt. In 2·1010 steps every gap met there is odd. The counter built from these rules (a chain of units, each a quarter as fast as the one before) is described from the run but not yet proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 46,428 cells have been visited and 32,888 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.48×10<sup>15</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 2,482,693,369,154,826 without a halt (the run stopped there because the tape no longer compresses into few enough runs of blocks). At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,009,883 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Runs growing at powers of 4
claims.text: At the left-end visits in state B, the run (110101)^a grows from 2,464 to 6,464 words between 1.9·108 and 1.26·109 steps (one per 4 rounds), (011101)^c from 604 to 1,604 (one per 16) and a second (110101)^b from 143 to 393 (one per 64).

claims.title: Block rules of the two passes
claims.text: Pass to the right (1 D> 1 1^a): a next block of b ≥ 3 cells is erased, leaving b − 2 zeros, and the pass restarts on the block after it, now 4 longer (r_step, r_step_3, r_step_4, r_step1); a next block of 2 is merged (r_merge); a next block of 1 turns the head (r_bounce). Sweep to the left (C and B on alternate cells): every other 1 is erased (l_sweep), a single 0 is filled (l_gap1), a gap of two or more turns the head (l_turn, b_turn7); the wall is crossed n words at a time (wall_l). For all values of the parameters.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: 1 0 0 0 0 B> 1 (B on the leftmost 1 of a block with exactly four 0s on its left) reaches A on a 1 in 7 steps.

claims.title: The rules against the run, 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: Of the 7.1·10<sup>8</sup> passes to the right, all but 168 start under one of the proved rules, and the block erased is always odd (never 2 or 4 cells). B stands on the leftmost 1 of a block 123 times, with 1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 17, 55 or more than 59 zeros on its left, never 4. After step 193,799,086 the head keeps a fixed parity in each of the states A, B, C, E (C and A on even cells, B on odd ones) and comes no closer than 182 cells to the right end of the tape.

claims.title: A chain of base-4 units
claims.text: Read at the left end, the tape is a fixed prefix, then units: a wall (110101)^n followed by a digit with four phases. A unit advances one phase when the unit before it has gone through its four, and its wall gains two words per cycle. At 3·109 steps the walls have 9989, 2486, 614, 113, 27 and 4 words. New units appear at the far end of the chain, in front of a last stretch of about 250 cells that has not changed since step 7.4·108.

claims.title: Block rules of the two passes
claims.text: Pass to the right (1 D> 1 1^a): a next block of b ≥ 3 cells is erased, leaving b − 2 zeros, and the pass restarts on the block after it, now 4 longer (r_step, r_step_3, r_step_4, r_step1); a next block of 2 is merged (r_merge); a next block of 1 turns the head (r_bounce). Sweep to the left (C and B on alternate cells): every other 1 is erased (l_sweep), a single 0 is filled (l_gap1), a gap of two or more turns the head (l_turn, b_turn7); the wall is crossed n words at a time (wall_l). For all values of the parameters.

claims.title: The halting pattern
claims.text: 1 0 0 0 0 B> 1 (B on the leftmost 1 of a block with exactly four 0s on its left) reaches A on a 1 in 7 steps.

claims.text: Of the 7.1·10<sup>8</sup> passes to the right, all but 168 start under one of the proved rules, and the block erased is always odd (never 2 or 4 cells). B stands on the leftmost 1 of a block 123 times, with 1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 17, 55 or more than 59 zeros on its left, never 4. After step 193,799,086 the head keeps a fixed parity in each of the states A, B, C, E (C and A on even cells, B on odd ones) and comes no closer than 182 cells to the right end of the tape.

claims.text: Read at the left end, the tape is a fixed prefix, then units: a wall (110101)^n followed by a digit with four phases. A unit advances one phase when the unit before it has gone through its four, and its wall gains two words per cycle. At 3·109 steps the walls have 9989, 2486, 614, 113, 27 and 4 words. claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Missing: the rules of a whole round through a chain of units of any length (digit phases, the carry between units, the birth of a new top unit), and an invariant closed under them that keeps every gap met by B odd. The run to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps (and an outside accelerated run to 10<sup>17</sup>, not checked here) shows no halt.

explainer.lede: Probably never halts, but not proved. The machine keeps a counter in base 4 whose digits sit between growing walls of a six-cell word; Lean proves how the head rewrites blocks of 1s on its way right and left; the only way to the halt is to meet a gap of exactly four 0s, which the run never does.

sections.heading: Two passes over blocks of 1s
html: Read the tape as blocks of 1s separated by 0s. The head does two things in turn.

A pass to the right. In state D the head runs to the end of its block, erases the last two cells of it and the whole next block, and starts again on the block after that, which it first makes four cells longer. So every other block becomes a gap of 0s (a block of b cells leaves b − 2 zeros). The pass ends when the block to erase is a single 1: the head turns.

A sweep to the left. In states C and B, on alternate cells, the head erases every other 1 (a block becomes 1 0 1 0 1). A single 0 between blocks is filled and the sweep goes on; at a wider gap the head turns and a new pass to the right starts two cells further left.

In the wall, blocks of 3 and 1 alternate (...1 0 111 0 1 0 111..., the word 110101). The pass to the right turns it into blocks of 5 with single 0s, and the sweep to the left turns those back into the wall, shifted. Lean proves each of these rules for all block lengths.

sections.heading: A gap of exactly four
html: The halting transition is A reading a 1. A is entered only from E on a 0, E only from D on a 0, and following the table back the only way there is the sweep to the left arriving in state B on the leftmost 1 of a block with exactly four 0s to its left (halt4 in Lean shows this pattern does halt).

The gaps are made by the pass to the right, b − 2 zeros from a block of b cells, and in the run every erased block is odd, so every gap is odd. In 2·1010 steps B stands on the leftmost 1 of a block only 123 times, the last at step 193,799,085, with 1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 17, 55 or more zeros on its left. What is missing for a proof is an invariant that says which blocks can ever be erased.

sections.heading: A counter that grows new digits
html: Seen from the left end, the tape is a fixed prefix followed by a chain of units. Each unit is a wall of the word 110101 and, after it, a short pattern with four phases: a digit. The first digit moves one phase per round (a round is one trip of the head from the left end and back) and its wall gains a word every second round; the second moves once every four rounds, the third every sixteen. At 3·109 steps the walls hold 9989, 2486, 614, 113, 27 and 4 words, each about a quarter of the one before.

Most rounds the head turns at the first digit and never sees the rest. The far end of the tape was last visited at step 193,765,310; since then new units have appeared at the end of the chain, and the last 250 cells or so are the same in samples from step 7.4·108 to 3·109. This is the shape of a counter that never halts, but the rules for a whole chain and for the birth of a unit are read off the run, not proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 46,428 cells (33,972 left of the start, 79 right), with a density of 1s of 0.708.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A chain of base-4 digits, each with a growing wall of 110101 words, that gains new top digits in front of a frozen last stretch of tape; block rules and the single halting pattern proved, the counter itself not yet.
